purpose: Independent, claim-by-claim audit of the registered findings in output/Result.md. Each claim is tied to (a) the authoritative result artifact(s) with the exact field path(s) and value(s), (b) the analysis source that produced them, (c) an independent re-derivation (output/analysis/independent_rederr.py -> output/results/independent_rederr.json), and (d) the supporting figure(s). The audit also records what was NOT verified and the residual limitations.

data_integrity.dedup_note: 70 exact replicated rows in 40 groups (max multiplicity 8) collapsed to 5920; every replicate carries identical pvalue and strength.

1_stage_trend_and_transport.claim: Within-unit-centred interaction strength rises across ordered stages (slope +0.0418/stage, CI [0.0293,0.0544], r=0.922), and the stage trend transports to held-out families (MAE 0.4681 -> 0.4275, -8.7%, permutation control).

result_evidence.claim_part: within-unit OLS slope +0.0418 per stage
family-clustered bootstrap 95% CI [0.0293, 0.0544]
stage-curve Pearson r = 0.922 (within-unit centred)
per-unit slopes: n=579, mean +0.0529, 72.7% positive, t(578)=9.27, p=3.5e-19, sign test 421 vs 158 p=1.4e-28
per-stage curve values (within-unit centred, stages 0..17)
leave-one-family-out holdout: MAE 0.4681 -> 0.4275, improvement 8.66%
permutation control: null improvement -0.0011 +/- 0.0004, observed +0.0406, p_two=0.00399 (500 perms)
permutation control (200 perms, independent code path 05): null -0.0011 +/- 0.0004, exceeds all
cell-pair holdout: MAE 0.4681 -> 0.4271, -8.74%
composition controls agree in sign: record-weighted r=0.79/+0.078, family-equal r=0.71/+0.061, post-stratified r=0.88/+0.076, within-unit r=0.92/+0.042
single most fragile variant: all-18-stage units slope +0.0258 (r=0.404)

figures.observed: Panel A: four curves (record-weighted grey dashed, family-equal blue, post-stratified red, within-unit centred green) all rise from low stage 0 to high stage 17; within-unit centred curve is the flattest and lowest in early stages (~0.4-0.5) and highest late, consistent with a +0.042/stage within-unit trend; record-weighted curve ends highest (~1.3). Panel B: strength histogram is strongly bimodal (a large mode near 0 and a smaller positive mode near +2) with a long right tail to ~6.3, consistent with a mixture of persistent family levels (SD 1.75, range [-3.51,6.30]).

Panel A: three bars - unit mean (null) 0.4681 (grey), unit mean + stage trend 0.4275 (green), unit mean + shuffled stage 0.4670 (red); the shuffled-stage bar is essentially at null, confirming the gain is not an artifact of the fit, and title states improvement 8.7%, permutation p < 0.0050. Panel B: scatter of per-family MAE gain vs held-out family size (log x); points straddle 0 both above and below, with a mild positive trend toward larger families, consistent with 102 improved / 112 worsened.

fields.F1_holdout_match: mae_null 0.4681, mae_trend 0.4275, improvement 8.7%, rmse 9.3% all match; cellpair mae_trend 0.4271 matches

independent_rederr_status.note: Independent stream reads the RAW tsv (not analysis_table.tsv) and recomputes with a separate implementation; agrees with the authoritative artifacts.

robustness_evidence.claim: 10 of 11 alternative trend definitions preserve sign/significance
family-clustered vs record-level inference: all CIs block on family

limitations: Stage indices are ordinal only, not metrically spaced; the per-stage 'rate' is a simplification.
Only 14 units span all 18 stages; the balanced-panel estimate (slope +0.0258, r=0.404) is materially weaker, so the trend is a distributional property, not a law.

Transport is real in aggregate but NOT uniform per family (102 improved / 112 worsened); per-family gains correlate with family size and stage coverage, so small/under-covered families are least reliably improved.
No technical covariate exists in the frozen table, so the trend cannot be separated from a stage-correlated technical drift.

2_identity_dominates_stage.claim: Interaction identity (family/unit), not stage, carries most of the structure: family explains 83.6% and unit 90.1% of record-level variance; stage ~1.8%.

result_evidence.claim_part: family share 0.836, unit share 0.901, stage share 0.018, cell-pair 0.040
record-level partition: between units 90.1%, within 9.9%, stage within-unit 1.8% (18.6% of within-unit slice)
family mean SD 1.43, size median 10, max 130
family mean strength correlates +0.58 with number of stages a family occupies
stage axis explains only 1.8% of total variance (partA_record_level_partition.share_stage_within_units)

figures.observed: Panel B (bimodal strength distribution created by the mixture of family levels) supports the claim that identity, not stage, creates the marginal structure.

fields.F2_family_share_match: family 0.836, unit 0.901, stage 0.018, family_mean_sd 1.43, size median 10, size max 130 all match

robustness_evidence.claim: label shuffling preserving family size collapses between-family variance to 0.722 (z=15.2, p<=0.002)
adjusting for stage composition retains 85% of raw between-family variance (z=13.8)
split-half reliability of family means r=0.834

limitations: 0.836 is a fixed-effects eta2 on unequal group sizes; a random-effects ICC is 0.829. The exact percentage is definition-dependent (both quoted).
Family identity correlates with panel coverage (+0.58), a genuine confound between 'how strong' and 'how well sampled'.
Identifiers are anonymous; no biological interpretation of 'families' is offered.

3_evidence_column_coarse_tier.claim: The association_pvalue column is a coarse floor/non-floor report tier, not a graded strength readout: 87.6% at floor 0.0009; the five non-floor levels are not ordered by strength; within-unit AUC 0.618.

result_evidence.claim_part: 6 discrete levels, floor share 87.6%
raw rho -0.285 (p~7e-111); within-unit -0.134 (p~3e-25); within-family -0.220 (p~1e-65)
non-floor only: rho -0.041, p=0.272 (n=736); within-unit non-floor rho +0.007, p=0.844
non-floor mean strength spans only 0.28 units vs global SD 1.75; Kruskal p=0.097
floor/non-floor contrast: paired within-unit diff +0.371, AUC 0.618, Cohen's d 0.383
tier does not track absolute magnitude: |dev| flat across tiers, Spearman -0.078
variance: full 6-tier explains 0.0176 of within-unit variance (raw 0.0743); floor split 0.016; non-floor 0.008

figures.observed: Panel A: % records at floor vs stage_index is non-monotone (rises 66% at stage 0 to a peak ~96% around stage 9, drops to ~76% at stage 14, back up to ~87% at 17) - the instrument's operating point drifts across stages. Panel B: mean strength by p-tier on log x; the floor tier (1e-3) has the highest raw mean (~0.81) while non-floor tiers (1e-2..5e-2) sit at or below ~0 and are non-monotone (0.04 highest, 0.05 lowest), within-unit centred line near zero - consistent with non-floor tiers carrying no ordered strength information.

fields.F3_floor_share_match: floor share 0.876, rho_raw -0.285, rho_within -0.134, rho_nonfloor -0.041, nonfloor range 0.28 all match

limitations: The floor value 0.0009 looks like a censoring floor; if so the true p-distribution is left-censored and the floor/non-floor contrast understates the real evidence difference - not verifiable from the frozen table.
The non-floor levels may encode a different quantity (e.g., per-stage detection threshold) that the table does not distinguish.

The main-analysis artifact evidence_coupling.json retains a buggy lability count (8/22/688); the correct count (360/22/336) is in evidence_tier.json.section4_lability and independent_rederr.json.F5_lability (see finding 5).

4_transience_and_heterogeneous_transport.claim: 210 of 579 multi-stage (>=3) units reverse sign (transient); the family holdout transport is heterogeneous: 102 of 214 families improve, 112 worsen (sign p=0.5385), per-family gain correlates +0.34 with family size and +0.40 with stage coverage.

transient count threshold-invariant: 210 across all 12 threshold points
sign instability corroborated: 491/718 multi-stage units constant sign, 227 reversing
heterogeneous transport: 102 improved / 112 worse / 0 tied, sign p=0.5385, n_families=214
per-family gain correlates +0.34 with family size, +0.40 with stage count
per-family MAE table (214 rows): null/trend MAE, improvement, improved/tied flags

figures.observed: Panel A: horizontal bar chart of 5 classes among 579 units (>=3 stages): persistent level 239 (green, longest), transient sign reversing 210 (red), unresolved flat 66 (grey), emerging 49 (blue), declining 15 (orange, shortest). Panel B: threshold sensitivity - transient sign reversing (red) is flat at ~211 across all slope thresholds (0.1/0.15/0.2/0.3), while persistent (green), unresolved (grey), emerging (blue), declining (orange) move a lot (e.g., persistent 104->319, emerging 90->4), illustrating that only the sign-reversing count is threshold-invariant.
Panel B: per-family MAE gain vs family size (log x); points straddle zero with a mild positive trend, title states 102 of 214 improve, 112 worsen.

fields.F4_per_family_match: 102 improved / 112 worsened / sign p=0.5385040002283777 match (independent recomputation reads RAW tsv, vectorised leave-one-family-out, matches authoritative 13_holdout_replication.json)

limitations: 'Transient' = sign reversal of a value whose reliability is unmeasured (one value per unit-stage, no replicate). Cannot read as '36% of interactions genuinely switch on/off'.
Per-family gains for small families are estimated from very few records; the size correlation is partly a precision artefact.
Emerging/declining/persistent/unresolved counts are threshold-sensitive and should be read as illustrative, not estimates.

5_evidence_verdict_lability.claim: For the same unit across stages, strength is highly reproducible (split-half r=0.908) while the floor/non-floor evidence verdict is not (agreement 0.875, Cohen's kappa 0.122): 360 always-floor, 22 always-non-floor, 336 mixed of 718; P(floor next | floor now)=0.931, P(floor next | non-floor now)=0.708.

result_evidence.claim_part: state patterns: 360 always-floor, 22 always-non-floor, 336 mixed of 718; shares 0.501/0.031/0.468
transitions: P(floor next | floor now)=0.931, P(floor next | non-floor now)=0.708
split-half reliability: strength r=0.908 (>=2 obs per half 0.931); floor fraction r=0.372, kappa 0.122
unit-level clustering: chi2=1612, df=717, dispersion 2.25 vs i.i.d. expected 316 always-floor / 399 mixed
test-retest (>=4 stages): strength split-half r=0.924, floor-fraction r=0.372, kappa 0.199

figures.observed: Panel A shows the floor prevalence drifting non-monotonically across stages (consistent with a threshold-crossing account); Panel B shows the floor tier dominates in raw mean strength while within-unit centred means are near zero, consistent with the verdict being a coarse threshold flag rather than a stable strength readout.

fields.F5_lability_buggy_would_match_note: NEGATIVE CONTROL: the buggy 8/22/688 (NaN-pivot over all 18 stage columns) path does NOT reproduce the correct 360/22/336; this is intentionally false and is excluded from the all-headline roll-up.

limitations: The main-analysis artifact evidence_coupling.json.q2_evidence_stability still reports the buggy 8/22/688 count (a NaN-pivot artefact: sig.all(axis=1) over all 18 stage columns requires all 18 stages observed AND floor; only 14 units have all 18 stages, 8 of which are always-floor). The correct counts (360/22/336) are in evidence_tier.json.section4_lability, independent_rederr.json, and Result.md (Finding 5). The buggy artifact is retained for provenance and flagged in evidence_tier.json.section5_verdict.conflicts_with_stated_facts.
The 22 always-non-floor units are a small cell; statistics conditioning on them are unstable and not used.
Most likely mechanical explanation is a threshold-crossing artefact (no replicate measurements to test directly).

independent_rederr_rollup.how_computed: Flattens every positive match flag in summary (including nested per-check dicts F1_holdout_match, F2_family_share_match, F3_floor_share_match, F5_transition_match) and requires all to be true. It explicitly EXCLUDES the negative-control flag F5_lability_buggy_would_match, which is intentionally False (it asserts the buggy 8/22/688 path does not reproduce the correct 360/22/336). This flag is a check on bug-detection, not a headline number in Result.md, so it must not force the roll-up to False.

figure_review.method: All four PNGs were visually inspected with the Read tool (one by one). Observations are recorded here and are consistent with the numeric artifacts.

F1_stage_trend_and_distribution.panel_A: Title 'Stage trend survives composition controls'. Four line series across stage_index 0..17: record-weighted (grey dashed), family-equal (blue), post-stratified (red), within-unit centred (green). All rise from low early stages to high late stages. Within-unit centred is the flattest/lowest in early stages (~0.4-0.5) and highest late (~1.0); record-weighted ends highest (~1.3). Consistent with a within-unit +0.042/stage trend and with the composition-confounding narrative (record-weighted curve inflated by large families present late).
F1_stage_trend_and_distribution.panel_B: Title 'Strength distribution SD=1.75, range [-3.51, 6.30]'. Strongly bimodal histogram: large mode near 0 (and a secondary peak slightly positive), a long right tail to ~6.3, small left tail to ~-3.5. Consistent with a mixture of persistent family-specific levels.
F1_stage_trend_and_distribution.consistency_with_report: Panel A supports Finding 1 (trend under multiple estimators); Panel B supports Finding 2 (mixture of family levels / identity-dominated structure).

F2_evidence_tier.panel_A: Title 'Evidence floor prevalence is non-monotone'. % records at floor 0.0009 vs stage_index: rises from ~66% at stage 0 to a plateau/peak ~92-96% (stages 5-9), dips to ~76% at stage 14, back to ~87% at stage 17. Non-monotone, consistent with the instrument's operating point drifting across stages (range 0.294).
F2_evidence_tier.panel_B: Title 'Non-floor tiers sit below the floor tier'. Mean strength by association_pvalue (log x, 6 discrete tiers). Two series: raw mean (blue circles) and within-unit centred (green squares). Raw mean highest at floor (~0.81), drops to ~-0.55 at 0.01 and ~-0.76 at 0.05; non-floor points are non-monotone. Within-unit centred line is near zero across all tiers (floor ~0.02, non-floor -0.2 to -0.3). Consistent with non-floor tiers carrying no ordered within-unit strength information.
F2_evidence_tier.consistency_with_report: Supports Finding 3 (coarse floor/non-floor tier, non-ordered above floor) and Finding 5 (threshold drift / lability).

F3_trajectory_taxonomy.panel_A: Title 'Trajectory taxonomy'. Horizontal bars for 5 classes among 579 units (>=3 stages): persistent level 239 (green, longest), transient sign reversing 210 (red), unresolved flat 66 (grey), emerging 49 (blue), declining 15 (orange, shortest). Matches trajectories_holdout.json.partA_taxonomy.class_counts.
F3_trajectory_taxonomy.panel_B: Title 'Threshold sensitivity'. Units assigned vs slope threshold (0.1/0.15/0.2/0.3; flat-SD varied 0.30/0.50/0.75). transient sign reversing (red) is flat at ~211 across all thresholds (threshold-invariant); persistent (green), unresolved (grey), emerging (blue), declining (orange) move a lot (persistent 104->319, emerging 90->4). Consistent with the claim that only the sign-reversing count is robust.
F3_trajectory_taxonomy.consistency_with_report: Supports Finding 4 (210 transient, threshold-invariant; other classes threshold-sensitive).

F4_holdout_transport.panel_A: Title 'Family-holdout MAE improvement 8.7%, permutation p < 0.0050'. Three bars: unit mean (null) 0.4681 (grey), unit mean + stage trend 0.4275 (green), unit mean + shuffled stage 0.4670 (red). Shuffled-stage bar ~null, confirming the gain comes from the real stage trend, not the fit. Consistent with holdout_replication.json (MAE 0.4681->0.4275, -8.7%).
F4_holdout_transport.panel_B: Title 'Transport is heterogeneous 102 of 214 improve, 112 worsen'. Scatter of per-family MAE gain (y, -0.4 to +0.4) vs held-out family size (log x, records). Points straddle 0 both above and below, with a mild positive trend toward larger families. Consistent with 102 improved / 112 worsened and the size correlation +0.34.

residual_limitations_and_honesty_notes: The frozen table has one value per unit-stage with no replicates; measurement noise and true variation are not separable. This bounds Findings 4 and 5.
No external data or literature was used; all evidence is from data/stage_indexed_interactions.tsv. No T0 source-date verification was required because no external source was used.
Identifiers are anonymous; stage indices are ordinal, not metrically spaced; no causal or mechanistic claim is made.

One artifact (evidence_coupling.json.q2_evidence_stability) intentionally retains a known-incorrect lability count (8/22/688) for provenance; the correct count (360/22/336) is the one used in the report and independent stream. This is documented, not hidden.

The sign-test p-value in the per-family heterogeneity claim was corrected in Result.md from a stale '102 vs 111 excluding one floating-point tie, p=0.58' to the authoritative '102 vs 112, p=0.5385' (no tie in holdout_replication.json.per_group_summary / leave_one_family_out_per_family).

The all_headline_numbers_reproduce flag was corrected: the previous roll-up only looked at top-level bools (skipping nested match dicts) and let the intentionally-False negative control F5_lability_buggy_would_match force it to False. It now flattens all positive match flags and excludes the negative control.
